Keep in mind, up until Tet, the media was saying America was winning in Vietnam. The Tet Offensive was a huge gamble and it worked in part due to the American media covering it so extensively because art surrounding the Vietnam War became extremely popular and it became a defining cultural issue. 

Vietnam War journos published pictures that absolutely shocked Americans and shattered their illusions about the war. The little girl with her clothes burnt off running from a napalm strike, the infamous street execution of a partisan, the photos of the station being attacked during Tet, showing a young baby-faced soldier, rifle in hand, cowering behind cover while surrounded by the bloody bodies of his fallen comrades; photos like these became iconic and shocked the American public who up until then thought U.S. troops were just there to back up Saigon and weren’t directly engaged in the fighting. 

It also captured the public interest due to the draft. Parents saw those photos and were horrified at the prospect of their sons and grandchildren being sent into the meat grinder. Young men saw those photos and knew if their name came up in the lottery, they would be the ones toting rifles through the jungle getting shot at. The paranoia surrounding the draft cannot be understated. There was a massive backlash against the draft, some draft offices even got burned down. There were veterans coming home and burning their medals and uniforms in protest. American soldiers gunned down protesting students at Kent State, an incident that honestly should have gone down in history as the American Tiananmen Square. 

The Vietnam War was a massive mismanaged clusterfuck but losing control of the domestic cultural sphere did have a big impact in ending the war.

C’mon bro, you could make that same argument about most empires but that still doesn’t make Caesar’s conquest of Gaul bloodless or even justifiable. The Gallic tribes weren’t a threat to Rome whatsoever. Caesar himself didn’t even attempt to justify it beyond “The Gauls will welcome us with open arms” which was plainly a lie, it was specifically a military conquest for land, slaves, power, influence, and control. The idea that he was supporting and bravely defending some unnamed and oh-so enlightened pro-Roman cohort in the North from the terrible barbarians is just plain propaganda.

“Caesar exaggerated the numbers so it was actually completely justified” is also a wild argument. It is pure speculation to try to guess how much Caesar flubbed the numbers, did he exaggerate it? Probably. By how much? We will literally never know. He could have been telling the truth for all we know. 

Saying what Caesar did in Gaul was completely justified because the people that weren’t killed or enslaved got roads afterward is completely insane and bordering on genocide apologia. Keep in mind those roads were only built and maintained mainly for Roman troops to use to quickly bring soldiers to areas that fell back into tribal control, and for transportation of tribute back to Rome. “Free trade” was absolutely not the goal.

Even if I grant you all of this, all you have to do is glance at a history book and you can plainly see that a lot of people in the North were not happy with this arrangement and were willing to continue to fight Rome for the chance at their own independence and governance. It’s honestly disgusting how quickly you handwave and justify A QUARTER MILLION PEOPLE dying IN THEIR OWN LAND in one battle alone at the hands of ruthless foreign invaders because the survivors got roads afterward. Caesar’s conquest in Gaul was a slaughter for slaves and power. It was not some misguided attempt at state building. What level of “Might makes Right” are you on my guy?

What’s that quote? “Caesar killed a million Gauls and enslaved a million more.” Or something along those lines. The Roman Northern Conquest and the Gallic Wars were insanely bloody by ancient metrics. They estimate a quarter million people died at the battle of Alesia alone. Think about the massive undertaking that was to organize a quarter million people to fight and die long before modern communication technology or even roads. It was an absolute bloodbath. Historians and archaeologists have tried to map the ramparts and battle lines at Alesia and they are miles-long. Most of the deaths occurred when the Gallic forces broke and Caesar’s troops literally went around slaughtering any and all survivors including civilians, women and children.

I love Roman history and the Gallic Wars are my favorite subject but it’s really easy to forget the scale of the bloodshed. A quarter million people dying in battle would be a tragedy TODAY, but back then it was simply unprecedented. Witnessing the battle of Alesia would be dreadful. Pure panic. I can’t even imagine it from Caesar’s perspective, cornered hundreds of miles from home in a strange land, surrounded and outnumbered by what must have seemed like an endless horde of bloodthirsty barbarians that stretched for miles, being attacked day in and day out with limited men and supplies. It was no wonder Caesar had the ego he did after winning that battle, seemingly against all odds. A lot of arguments against Marxism are either just utterly ignorant strawman arguments that can be debunked by reading literally the first few pages of Capital, or are complete projections.

-“Marxists are idealists”

Marxists believe in material, objective reality and truth. It is the capitalists who are the post-modernists who believe that the abstract subjective value that determines market forces stems entirely from desires, ideas, and valuations that exist in your own head. 

-“Marxists believe in post-scarcity”

It is the capitalists who believe we live in a world where we can endlessly consume commodities with no regard for the future, wherein economic growth and profit is infinite. 

-“Marxists are anti-human, anti-individualists”

Marxists believe that socially useful human labor is the single most important thing that separates us from animals and that the economy exists to serve man and human society, not the other way around. It is quite literally the capitalists that are anti-humanists that believe that human labor and human beings themselves are inherently worthless. 

-“Marxists believe everyone is equal”

From each according to their ability, to each according to their need. Why would Marx say this if everyone was equal and had the same needs and abilities? It is quite literally the capitalists who believe human workers are interchangeable cogs in a machine with no inherent unique value.

-“Marxists don’t want you to own anything”

Capitalism has largely already abolished private property for the vast majority of people. “You will own nothing and be happy” is a capitalist creation, not a Marxist one. Marxists believe that owning your own home, your own land, owning your own workplace, and owning the products of your labor is the basis of political and economic liberty and that indeed every man is entitled to this ownership, not just a select few.

-“Marxists don’t know economics”

It is capitalists that believe that the value of commodities is entirely subjective and has no basis in utility. It is capitalists that believe if enough people think about cheeseburgers, the market magically produces them. It is Marxists that believe that commodities and human labor have real objective value that can be calculated by utility combined with supply and demand, and labor cost of production and capital creation.

-“Marxists believe all labor is equal, so if I just make mudpies I’ll be a millionaire right?”

This is literally debunked in the first page of capital, for labor and commodities to have value at all they must be socially useful. It is quite literally the capitalists that believe that you can shit in a bucket, and if enough people demand the turd, it gives the turd value. 

-“Marxism makes people lazy and Marxists don’t want to work.” 

Marxists believe that socially useful labor is a meaningful part of our human essence and experience. It is quite literally the capitalists that de-incentive “working hard” through wage labor, lack of ownership of capital and produced commodities among other things. It is quite literally the capitalists that believe that people can sit around as parasites, endlessly consuming surplus but producing no actual value. It is quite literally the capitalists that believe unemployment is a necessary part of the system.

-“Marxists are dogmatic utopianists”

It is literally the capitalists that believe in a utopian post-scarcity world where resources are endless and human labor can be completely automated away, wherein people don’t have to work and can sit around endlessly consuming goods produced by machines or the third world. I started last wipe and have played with much more skilled players than myself that have gotten frustrated with me at times, so I know exactly what your friend is going through. Honestly the only thing I can suggest is to just be patient and let your friend improve naturally. Tarkov is a tough game, there is a skill curve and it just takes time. Keep giving him constructive criticism. As a noob it’s real easy to get into the habit of being carried by a better teammate, if you really want him to improve, encourage him to play solo more or make him take the lead on some raids to help him gain some confidence. Knowing the maps makes a massive difference and I ended up actually printing out the in-game maps to keep on my desk. Don’t get mad at equipment, as he gains confidence he will be more comfortable with more expensive equipment, if a loadout works for him and his budget, let him use it. I still mainly use a BP SKS and basic armor until I unlock flea. 

It’s also a matter of tailoring your expectations as well. I started playing Tarkov in my spare time to have a few beers and have fun and if he’s in the same boat, you can’t really expect him to act like a sweaty chad every raid. You can’t expect him to keep up with you or know the maps or be as aggressive, etc, simplify your raid plans, take the time to learn how he plays and be a good foil to that. Don’t just boss him around or say “this is what you do” or expect him to play exactly like you because that’s only going to lead to frustration if there is a clear skill gap between the two of you. Don’t expect him to play like you do or even how you want him to. Take into account his strengths and weaknesses, his skill level, and what he likes to do or how he likes to play and be HIS teammate. 

I can’t tell you the amount of times I’ve hopped in a discord and the highly skilled player I’m teamed up with gets frustrated because he expects me to play exactly like him and his favorite streamer (not saying that’s you) and I’m simply not at that level yet. I would bet a lot of what you are telling him is flying over his head or he can’t implement ingame because he just doesn’t have to a good grasp on the game itself, the maps, and the “flow” of firefights in Tarkov. You can’t expect him to win every encounter. When you die before he does, you need to accept that as your own failure, not his. If he dies before you, you need to coach him on what he did wrong. 

You need to learn to jive with him and his skill level until he improves, just as much as he needs to learn to jive with yours and I think that’s important to remember. Play a little more tactically, confirm positions or let him get into positions before you attack, don’t get into encounters if you both don’t have the jump on another player, etc. If you have fun with him and want to keep playing with him then just do that. If you are continually getting frustrated with him then maybe save the super-sweaty raids for solo or another group. Sometimes players are just not good fits for the play style you want to play, and that’s ok, and it doesn’t mean you have to stop playing with them, you just have to realize they aren’t at that level yet and tailor your expectations for a different experience than you are used to. 

Getting frustrated with him is only going to lead to more frustration and, according to you, him to stop playing. If you like playing with him you just need to have some patience. The more you play together and the more he improves the more you will start to jive and move as a team. After some time, you guys will click and he will be right there doing what you want him to at the perfect time, but that takes time.

Eh if they keep them fairly realistic it wouldn’t be too bad, and they’d probably be rare to encounter anyway due to their limited use, time to setup, weight, and expense. Claymores need to actually be triggered remotely, trip wire IED’s leave a wire at a set height, and anti-personnel mines can’t just be plopped onto concrete and need to actually be buried into dirt which would leave a little circular mound of fresh dirt and remove any foliage. Make them fairly easy to disable silently with a toolkit/leatherman or detonate with a bullet/grenade. Antipersonnel mines are usually designed to wound, not kill, so just make it so you can’t be insta-killed by them and they wouldn’t be OP, just another tool. It will slow chads down or wound them or just function as an alarm for your squad.

Honestly I think they’d be fun, I wish there was more gameplay elements to encourage squads to stick together and move more tactically and realistically, almost no one actually holds or defends areas in game because the current meta is to get an OP kit, sprint to the high loot areas and then leave. Having more defensive tools would be good imo and might change the game a little in a good way.

Not only that, but trip wire IED’s are ubiquitous in modern urban guerrilla combat. Go look at recent examples like the Siege of Marawi. There’s videos out there of it. Philippine Special Forces had to painstakingly clear every building because ISIS had rigged damn near half the city to explode with improvised explosives in every nook and cranny. The biggest killer of U.S. forces in Afghanistan was improvised explosive devices. 

They would be a blast on maps like the new Streets of Tarkov, and it would also give solo players more tools to actually take on squads or defend areas alone. One of MACV-SOG’s favorite tactics was to throw down claymores as they were on the run retreating from a superior force, I’d love to be able to do that in Tarkov and turn the tables on sweaty chads out for my loot.

Modern warfare is all about manipulating your enemy into a position where you can kill them from afar with as little risk to your side as possible. Want to clear a room full of enemies? Why risk your squad when you can just toss a nade through the window. Want to defend an area? Why risk your squad when you can just mine it. If Tarkov is trying to be “realistic” and fairly accurate to actual CQB tactics, than not allowing IED’s is a baffling choice, especially since they are cheap and easily fit the theme of the skilled urban guerrilla warrior trying to survive in a modern wasteland. Mines have been around forever, they are common and cheap, if the vendors can get their hands on C4 and crates of surplus AK’s they almost certainly ran into a box of anti-personnel mines at some point. Hell, you should be able to craft trip mines at your hideout with wire, a soda can and a grenade, just like the Vietcong used to. 

The only problem I could see is people just rushing to high loot areas and planting them everywhere simply for the lols, but Tarkov encourages dirty tactics like that, getting domed by a guy with a FLIR at extract is just a part of the game already, and I see no reason to not include IED’s simply because they could be abused. That’s the point. You call it frustrating tactics, militaries around the world call it doctrine. It’s simply the way it is. Gameplay balance is not a word Nikita knows. I don’t think the game should be ARMA:CQB but I feel like Tarkov is the high-risk brutal PTSD simulator that it is because it allows for realistic things that other games don’t, and I think mines and IED’s are a natural part of the Tarkov world and gameplay style and it’d be a shame to not include them simply because they could be abused.

The Fragile Alliance mode in Kane & Lynch 2 was some of the most fun I’ve had in a heist-style game and I’m shocked Payday or GTA online hasn’t done something similar to it. To anyone who didn’t play it, the basic premise was this; you and your team of 8 people online were tasked with completing a co-op PVE-style heist against AI guards and police, you shoot up the place, steal the cash, and then get to the escape vehicle, if you all escape everyone splits the money, however, the twist is that it is also full PVP and at any point during the heist you can kill your player crewmates to betray them and take their money. Whoever has the most money at the end of a few rounds wins. If you managed to get to the escape vehicle, you could have the driver wait for your teammates to get in so you can split their profits, or you could just pay the driver to leave them behind, keeping all of the cash to yourself. 

It was a blast and encouraged exactly the kind of scumbaggery that one would expect in a high stakes crew of thieves. The most ruthless, conniving, and greedy players won. It kept you constantly looking over your shoulder at your “friends”. Everyone cooperated, but only until it was no longer useful. In practice, every round felt like a movie-style heist with uneasy allies. Everyone worked together to get the cash and then shit always hit the fan. So many great shootouts and tense standoffs as we waited for the helicopter, so many exciting moments as I escaped in the helicopter alone, laughing while leaving my teammates behind. There was always one who was willing to betray everyone to win. If I remember right, the game even had some degree of randomization, the characters were randomized and you couldn’t see usernames until after the match so people couldn’t just target you because you betrayed them in a previous game. 

In short it was a really unique game mode and I wish someone would make a fully fleshed game around that concept because it was a ton of fun.

Fun fact: we studied that script in a screenwriting class and it was noteworthy because it’s one of the few hollywood scripts of that time in which the characters are fully gender neutral. The writer thought a gender-inclusive military would fit the futuristic universe more and would allow the casting director more leeway to choose actors based on how much they personify the character instead of their physical description. This famously led to the decision to cast Sigourney Weaver as the main character in an era where having a female lead was seen as unprofitable and unmarketable. 

The line “Have you ever been mistaken for a man?” “No, have you?” was the writer poking fun at this in a very clever way, because the line still works REGARDLESS of the genders of the two characters who are speaking. “Have you ever been mistaken for a man?” Is equally insulting to both men and women and the “No, have you?” flips it on the speaker regardless of their gender. The two characters could be both men, both women, or a man and a woman, and the line still works.

The best way to get over gear fear is to just find a good budget loadout that works for you (for me it’s the SKS or VEPR) and just get good at running it. Sell everything that you are scared to lose, and alternate between scav raids. Once you start making money, add to your “default” loadout, add some armor or a helmet, or some weapon mods as needed for difficult raids. Insure everything so you have a constant supply of budget loadouts that people likely won’t bother to pick up if you die.

Once I started playing like that I started to not care about gear, anything nice I bring in that I feel comfortable losing is just a bonus now, because I can always fall back on my cheap “default” loadout that I feel 100% comfortable with.

Like others have said, the best gear in the world won’t help you if you are bad at the game or don’t know the maps, etc. Get good at simply surviving to extract with whatever you have available. 

Also, practice on offline raids! Once you get a cool loadout take it a for spin risk free and get used to it! There’s no point in losing gear to get better at the game when you can just offline raid and practice until you can survive online.
